narrative:
The model determined that you have a 27% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the length of the loan you requested, your credit history, and the status of your checking account. The short six-month duration you asked for actually worked in your favor, as it is far below the average of 19 months among approved applicants and pulled the prediction toward good credit. Your credit history, listed as critical or other existing credits, also pushed the outcome in a positive direction compared with many approved customers.

Unfortunately, the status of your checking account had the opposite and ultimately decisive effect. Your account being in negative balance (<0 DM) is relatively uncommon. Only 12.6% of all applicants show this status, and it strongly signaled higher risk to the model, outweighing the protective effects of the shorter duration and your credit history. This single factor was the main reason your application crossed the threshold for denial.

To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying. Even a modest improvement here could substantially strengthen future applications. Consider waiting until your account reflects more stable finances, then try again with a similar short-term request.
